result.topic_en: Euler applies his interpolation formula to sines. He takes ordinates p = sin nθ, q = sin(n+1)θ, … and obtains a general series; for θ = π and n = 1/2 he derives an integral Δ = (1+2ω)π/cos ωπ. He then warns that the interpolating curve need not be the sine curve itself.
result.transcription:
denominatorem applicatae respondentis datae euanescere, ita vt prae eo termino, quippe infinito, reliqui euanescant. Verum tum simul quoque valor $\Delta$ prodit infinitus, et praecise eiusmodi, vt tum fiat vel $y=p$, vel $y=q$, vel $y=r$, etc. quemadmodum rei natura postulat.

Corollarium 1.

§. 31. Si abscissae propositae denotent arcus circulares, applicatae vero eorundem sinus, vt sit
$p=\sin. n\theta,\ q=\sin.(n+1)\theta,\ r=\sin.(n+2)\theta$, etc.
erit $y=\sin.\omega\theta$, vnde ista resultat aequatio generalis:
$\frac{n\Delta\sin.\omega\theta}{2(n+\omega)\omega}=\frac{\sin.n\theta}{nn-\omega\omega}-\frac{2n}{1}\cdot\frac{\sin.(n+1)\theta}{(n+1)^2-\omega^2}+\frac{2n(2n+1)}{1\cdot 2}\cdot\frac{\sin.(n+2)\theta}{(n+2)^2-\omega^2}-\frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)}{1\cdot 2\cdot 3}\cdot\frac{\sin.(n+3)\theta}{(n+3)^2-\omega^2}$ etc.
vbi imprimis notatu est dignum, quod tres litterae, $n$, $\theta$ et $\omega$, pro lubitu accipi queant.

Corollarium 2.

§. 32. Si ergo sumamus $\theta=\pi$, vt omnes seriei sinus ad eundem $\sin. n\theta$ reducantur, erit
$\frac{n\Delta\sin.\omega\pi}{2(n+\omega)\omega\sin.n\pi}=\frac{1}{nn-\omega\omega}+\frac{2n}{1}\cdot\frac{1}{(n+1)^2-\omega^2}+\frac{2n(2n+1)}{1\cdot 2}\cdot\frac{1}{(n+2)^2-\omega^2}+\frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)}{1\cdot 2\cdot 3}\cdot\frac{1}{(n+3)^2-\omega^2}$ etc.
Hinc si fit
$n=\frac{1}{2}$ et $\Delta=\int z^{-\omega-\frac{1}{2}}dz(1-z)^{-\omega-\frac{1}{2}}$ [?], seu
$\Delta=2\int\frac{z^{\frac{1}{2}-\omega}dz}{(1-z)^{\frac{1}{2}+\omega}}$ [?], habebitur:
$\frac{\Delta\sin.\omega\pi}{2(1+2\omega)\omega}=\frac{4}{1-4\omega^2}+\frac{4}{9-4\omega^2}+\frac{4}{25-4\omega^2}+\frac{4}{49-4\omega^2}+$ etc. [?]
cuius seriei summam ostendi esse $=\frac{\pi}{2\omega}\,\mathrm{tang.}\,\omega\pi$, ita vt sit
$\frac{\Delta\sin.\omega\pi}{2(1+2\omega)\omega}=\frac{\pi}{2\omega}\,\mathrm{tang.}\,\omega\pi$, ideoque $\Delta=\frac{(1+2\omega)\pi}{\cos.\omega\pi}$.

Scholion 1.

§. 33. His autem conclusionibus nimium confidere non licet, ob rationem iam supra allegatam: Positis enim applicatis
$p=\sin.n\theta,\ q=\sin.(n+1)\theta,\ r=\sin.(n+2)\theta$, etc.
dum arcus $n\theta$, $(n+1)\theta$, $(n+2)\theta$ etc. vt abscissae spectantur, aequatio inuenta eiusmodi lineam curuam praebet, quae per omnia haec puncta transit; neque vero hinc sequitur, hanc curuam ipsam esse lineam sinuum, cum infinitae aliae dentur lineae curuae per eadem illa puncta infinita data transeuntes. Quare seruata littera $y$ pro applicata, abscissae $x=\theta\omega$ respondente, significanda, solutio nostra pro curua quaesita hanc quidem suppeditat aequationem:
$\frac{n\Delta y}{2(n+\omega)\omega}=\frac{\sin.n\theta}{n^2-\omega^2}-\frac{2n}{1}\cdot\frac{\sin.(n+1)\theta}{(n+1)^2-\omega^2}+\frac{2n(2n+1)}{1\cdot 2}\cdot\frac{\sin.(n+2)\theta}{(n+2)^2-\omega^2}-\frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)}{1\cdot 2\cdot 3}\cdot\frac{\sin.(n+3)\theta}{(n+3)^2-\omega^2}+$ etc.
ita vt abscissae $x=(n\pm i)\theta$ respondeat haec applicata: $y=\sin.(n\pm i)\theta$, si modo $i$ sit numerus integer quicunque. Fieri vero posset, vt pro aliis abscissis, vbi $i$ non est numerus integer, ideoque generatim si $x=\omega\theta$, non foret applicata $y=\sin.\omega\theta$. Quo hoc clarius perspiciatur, intelligemus aequationem generalem pro omnibus plane lineis per puncta data transeuntibus, sicque valor hactenus repertus $y=\Theta$, et quaeratur functio pro omnibus abscissis datis euanescens, cuiusmodi est

items.english: I have shown that the sum of this series is π/(2ω)·tan ωπ, so that Δ sin ωπ/(2(1+2ω)ω) = π/(2ω)·tan ωπ, and hence Δ = (1+2ω)π/cos ωπ.

items.english: But one must not trust these conclusions too much, for the reason already given above.

items.english: It could happen that for other abscissas, where i is not an integer, and so in general if x = ωθ, the ordinate would not be y = sin ωθ.

items.quote: Quo hoc clarius perspiciatur, intelligemus aequationem generalem pro omnibus plane lineis per puncta data transeuntibus, sicque valor hactenus repertus $y=\Theta$, et quaeratur functio pro omnibus abscissis datis euanescens
items.english: To see this more clearly, we shall consider the general equation for all lines whatever passing through the given points. Let the value found so far be y = Θ, and let a function be sought that vanishes for all the given abscissas.
